reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight centers on the interplay between risk and uncertainty, where the former implies measurable variability while the latter denotes unknowns. The indifference principle allows us to treat unobserved variables as neutral, enabling probabilistic modeling. This leads to a dual structure: one layer assumes uniformity among unseen causes (GSI's Bayesian inference), and another treats transitions as stochastic processes (GSE's dynamic modeling). Failure modes arise when systematic biases or non-random influences disrupt these assumptions—such as in free will debates or when deterministic forces override probabilistic outcomes. These primitives form a foundational basis for both statistical inference and agent-based simulation frameworks.
